PHASE.NAME: UPGRADE_5 User-Defined MCP Tools
PHASE.GOAL: Allow local user-defined command tools from ~/.synapse/tools while preserving MCP safety, built-in tool integrity, and token economy controls.

DATA_FLOWS.FLOW: User tool JSON definitions are loaded from ~/.synapse/tools, validated, and rejected if they override built-in MCP tools.
tools/list merges built-in tool definitions and user tool schemas, marking user tools with source metadata.
tools/call dispatches user command tools through timeout-bounded execution, path allowlists, ANSI stripping, and max output token caps.
syn tools list, validate, and new support local authoring without recompiling Synapse.

STEPS.step-1: Implement user tool definition model, loader, schema validation, built-in name protection, and warning collection.
STEPS.step-2: Implement command interpolation, allowed-path validation, timeout handling, ANSI stripping, and output token trimming.
STEPS.step-3: Merge user tools into tools/list with source metadata and compatible terse/full schema policies.
STEPS.step-4: Route unknown tools/call names to validated user tools after built-in dispatch misses.
STEPS.step-5: Add syn tools list, validate, and new commands with JSON-capable output.

VERIFICATION.CHECK: syn tools validate accepts a valid command tool and rejects built-in override names.
MCP tools/list includes user tools with source metadata.
MCP tools/call executes a user tool with timeout and max output token controls.

RISKS.RISK: User command tools can execute arbitrary local commands; first implementation must stay local-only and enforce timeout, path, and output controls.
Dynamic tools can bloat tools/list; reuse existing terse/profile disclosure and source metadata.
